meta.topic: Psyllium vs Inulin, Sunfiber (PHGG), Fenugreek & Acacia

slides.headline: Psyllium vs. Sunfiber vs. Inulin
slides.subhead: Which fiber is best for your product? A buyer-focused comparison of gel, bulk, and prebiotic fibers for supplements, drinks, and bakery.

slides.headline: Choose by what the product needs to do.
slides.subhead: Five common fibers, five different jobs. Here is the one-line rule for each.

rows.name: Psyllium husk
rows.rule: Gel, bulk, water binding, or a health claim — our lane.

rows.name: Sunfiber / PHGG
rows.rule: Clear, gentle, low-thickening fiber for beverages.

rows.name: Inulin / FOS
rows.rule: Prebiotic story where the dose stays tolerance-managed.

rows.name: Fenugreek
rows.rule: Viscous fiber with a metabolic story, if flavor allows.

rows.name: Acacia
rows.rule: Gentle soluble fiber where low gas beats gel strength.

rows.fit: Cholesterol, blood sugar, regularity — daily fiber with a health claim
Prebiotic, gut-microbiome support; easy food fortification
Clear-mixing prebiotic for beverages; well tolerated
Very gentle, low-gas prebiotic for sensitive guts

slides.statCaption: The FDA-recognized soluble fiber intake level associated with the authorized coronary-heart-disease risk-reduction claim.
slides.headline: Gel-forming, water-binding, barely fermented.
slides.body: A fit for cholesterol, blood-sugar, and regularity products that want gel, bulk, structure, and category access to a recognized health claim — the finished-brand owns the claim language.

slides.headline: The clear, low-thickening prebiotic.
bulletCards: Mixes invisibly — tasteless, no grit, no viscosity change in beverages.
No gel — so no cholesterol-type health claim.
slides.bestFit: Best fit: ready-to-drink beverages and gentle daily-fiber products where mixability beats gel.

cards.name: Inulin / FOS
cards.body: Strongest prebiotic story, nearly tasteless — but highly fermentable, so gas and bloating are common at higher doses.

cards.name: Fenugreek fiber
cards.body: Viscous, like psyllium, with an appetite/metabolic story — but a maple-like odor and legume-allergen labeling to manage.

cards.name: Acacia (gum arabic)
cards.body: Gentle, low-gas, dissolves clear — but very low viscosity, so no gel benefit and a higher dose is needed.

slides.headline: Work backwards from your claim.
slides.blendNote: Many products blend: psyllium for gel and claim, paired with a gentler prebiotic for microbiome support and tolerance. Always bench-test the blend.

caption.primaryText: Psyllium, Sunfiber (PHGG), inulin/FOS, fenugreek, and acacia are not interchangeable — each does a different job by function: gel-forming vs. prebiotic vs. low-viscosity mixability. Psyllium is the only one of the five carrying an FDA-recognized soluble fiber heart-health claim pedigree that a finished brand can build on. Choosing the right fiber starts with the claim or texture you're formulating for. RM Psyllium supports sample review and COA discussion before any order — export@rmpsyllium.com.
